Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fickle adjective

also shifty, unstable, unsteady, changeable

classical

Caes. BG 4.5: Gallī sunt in cōnsiliīs capiendīs mōbilēs (Lewis & Short: “changeable, inconstant, fickle”)
Traupman 157

mōbilis, mōbile

declension

movable; changeable, fickle

Other words

  • ventōsus, ventōsa, ventōsum — windy; changeable as the wind

    declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.8.12: Rōmae Tībur amem ventōsus, Tībure Rōmam (Lewis & Short: “light, changeable, inconstant, fickle”); Traupman 157

  • īnstabilis, īnstabile — unstable, changeable, fickle

    declension · also used · classical · Pac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.23.36: of Fortune, incerta īnstabilisque (Lewis & Short); Traupman 159, 400

  • incōnstāns, incōnstantis — inconstant, changeable, fickle

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Com. 6.19: mihi rīdiculē es vīsus esse incōnstāns (Lewis & Short)

  • cadūcus, cadūca, cadūcum — tottering; frail, fleeting

    declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 159, 400

    Traupman gives it for “unsteady (tottering)”, not for a fickle person: Lewis & Short has falling, and figuratively frail, fleeting, perishable (Cic. ND 1.35.98).
